speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; I understand you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress. To begin my assessment, how long has the difficulty breathing been occurring, and were there any complications during your birth?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information; the preterm gestation at 33 weeks and onset of distress 2 hours after birth strongly suggest a specific condition. Did you notice any "grunting," nasal flaring, or chest retractions while the baby was breathing, and did the mother have a history of Rho(D) incompatibility? speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood_Type_and_Coombs_test: Not available in provided data; Chest_X-Ray: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (NRDS).
